column1: Perhaps the most important contribution of the literature on time inconsistency, however, has been to provide theoretical frameworks for thinking formally about credibility issues, on the one hand, and the role of institutions and political factors, on the other, in influencing policy choices. By emphasizing the interactions of the incentives faced by policymakers, the structure of information about the economy and about the central bank’s preferences, and the public’s beliefs, the models examined in this chapter provide a critical set of insights that have influenced the recent debates over rules, discretion, and the design of monetary policy institutions.
